guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.description:
Observatory says 36.9C posted on Sunday is city’s highest official temperature since its records began 142 years ago, with storm driving intense heat in region

Hong Kong has officially recorded its highest ever temperature as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city, the meteorological service said.

The city’s weather observatory posted a temperature of 36.9C on Sunday, the highest recorded since records began in 1884, the Hong Kong Observatory said in the afternoon.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: France introduces tough fines for unsolicited telemarketing calls
rfi.description: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law to protect consumers and shield vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices. Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to €75,000 per call when the new law comes into effect on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Moscow and Damascus reach deal over Russian military bases in Syria
rfi.description: Syria said on Sunday it had reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.

rfi.title: Iran says ‘Muslim Nato’ pact reflects retreat from US security umbrella
rfi.description: Tehran has played down concerns over a new mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while portraying the agreement as evidence of declining regional reliance on the United States.

rfi.title: Record temperatures swept regions home to 900 million people in July
rfi.description: Regions home to around 900 million people experienced their hottest July on record in 2026, including areas in the Sahel, Central America, France and Spain, according to analysis of Copernicus data.

rfi.title: Ghana backs Jamaica's petition to push UK for slavery reparations
rfi.description: Jamaica and Ghana, both former British colonies subjected to the transatlantic slave trade, are presenting a united front in the drive for reparatory justice. As Kingston prepares to lodge a formal petition with King Charles III seeking to advance its claim for reparations from the United Kingdom, Ghana's president says the global movement to address the legacy of slavery has reached a "defining moment".

rfi.title: Outsiders Malawi beat Ghana to reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup
rfi.description: Malawi have completed one of the biggest surprises in Women’s Africa Cup of Nations history, coming from behind to beat Ghana 2-1 and secure both a place in the semi-finals and qualification for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

rfi.title: EU athletics to apply new TV guidelines on non-sexualisation of women
rfi.description: New guidelines to prevent broadcasters sexualising coverage of women athletes will come into place when the European championships start in Birmingham on Monday.

rfi.title: Netanyahu rejects Gaza plan in new break from Trump
rfi.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected a US-led Gaza plan endorsed by Hamas, putting distance between himself and President Donald Trump as he tries to shore up his base ahead of close elections.

rfi.title: As the planet heats up, butterflies are seeking out cooler climes
rfi.description: Climate change is driving shifts in where butterflies are found globally, according to a major new study, with some species moving northwards or seeking out higher elevations in search of cooler conditions.

rfi.title: Demi Vollering wins Women's Tour de France for the second time
rfi.description: Dutch cyclist Demi Vollering on Sunday won her second Women’s Tour de France title, dethroning defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot from France, who dropped out of the race on Saturday. Vollering excelled during the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney, who finished second overall.

rfi.title: Investigation raises alarm over uranium in DRC cobalt shipments to China
rfi.description: An investigation by Lighthouse Reports, The Financial Times and Le Monde traces the possible export of uranium from the Democratic Republic of Congo back to a confidential International Atomic Energy Agency memo obtained in 2024. Chinese mining group CMOC, which owns the main site examined in Katanga, disputes the findings.

rfi.title: Rise in injuries sees Paris police impose new rules on e-scooter users
rfi.description: Electric scooter riders in Paris must now wear helmets and reflective gear under new rules introduced after a significant rise in injuries involving the two-wheelers, police said at the weekend.

rfi.title: Sall's chances at UN secretary-general role weakened after first vote
rfi.description: Antonio Guterres’s successor as United Nations secretary-general will be named in October. So far, two candidates from the African continent – Senegal’s Macky Sall and Uganda’s Olara Otunnu – have failed to win sufficient support.

rfi.title: Morocco, Algeria reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup
rfi.description: A triumphant night for north Africa ended on Saturday with hosts Morocco and Algeria reaching the Women's Africa of Nations (WAFCON) semi-finals and the 2027 World Cup in Brazil.

euronews.title: Italy’s Po river runs low as drought threatens farms and water supplies
euronews.description: Italy’s Po River has fallen to historically low levels as the country endures its fourth heatwave of the summer, exposing wide stretches of dry riverbed near Pavia and raising fresh concerns over water supplies and farming across northern Italy.

euronews.description: Experts say overfishing, plastic pollution and warming seas due to climate change have created conditions allowing jellyfish to thrive and reproduce.

euronews.title: France’s oldest lumberjack contest puts axe skills to the test
euronews.description: France’s 73rd lumberjacking championship in Chamrousse saw 60 competitors race axes through logs, preserving Alpine forestry traditions for 2,000 spectators.

euronews.title: Extreme heat strains Italy's 'cheese banks,' where Parmigiano backs farm loans
euronews.description: Extreme heat is squeezing Italy's "cheese banks", the climate-controlled vaults in Emilia-Romagna where hundreds of thousands of Parmigiano Reggiano wheels sit as collateral for farm loans, pushing up energy bills and thinning the milk supply that fills them.

euronews.title: Mexican crews expected to arrive for wildfire fight in western Canada after 20,000 flee
euronews.description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police have opened a criminal investigation into the cause of the fire, which broke out on Friday.

euronews.description: Winegrowers say this year's harvest in Hungary's southernmost wine region will be smaller as dry heat forces early ripening, cutting yields.

euronews.description: The discovery of a motorbike wreck and the remains of two German soldiers is drawing global attention. Low Danube levels in Budapest exposed a WWII bike, now cleaned and remarkably well preserved.

Ernte: Landwirten im Nordosten drohen dunkle Wolken aus Brüssel
Tierschutz: Storch von Kirche geschossen - in Tierarztpraxis operiert
Verkehr: Brennender Lkw bei Rastatt - A5 Richtung Basel gesperrt
Drohnen am Flughafen Hannover: Drohne behindert Betrieb am Flughafen Hannover
zeit.description: Wenige Tage nach dem Drohnenfund am Flughafen Leipzig/Halle kam es auch in Hannover zu einer Sichtung. Der Flugbetrieb war am frühen Morgen kurzzeitig eingeschränkt.

zeit.title: »Entscheidung in Spanien« von Paul Ingendaay: Unter Blauäugigen und Blindwütigen
zeit.description: Von Simone Weil bis George Orwell: Im Spanischen Bürgerkrieg griffen auch Schriftsteller zur Waffe. Paul Ingendaay erzählt ihre Geschichten in einem glänzenden Panorama.

zeit.title: Opposition in Russland: Darf in Russland noch jemand gegen Putin antreten?
zeit.description: Die russische Oppositionspartei Jabloko ist doch nicht zur Parlamentswahl im September zugelassen. Kommt es jetzt zu Protesten? Und: Schweres Erdbeben in Kolumbien

zeit.title: Paarurlaub: »Es kann auch die Lösung sein, gar keinen Urlaub zusammen zu machen«
zeit.description: Wohin? Wer plant? Wann stehen wir auf? Urlaube stecken voller Konflikte. Paartherapeutin Sabine Heldner gibt Tipps, wie man mit Spannungen produktiv umgeht.

zeit.title: Rhein: Niedrigwasser am Rhein lässt Benzinpreise steigen
zeit.description: Die Pegelstände am Rhein sind aktuell historisch niedrig. Das treibt den Spritpreis. Vor allem in den westdeutschen Bundesländern ist Benzin derzeit wieder teurer.

france24fr.title: En rejetant le plan de Trump sur Gaza, Netanyahu offre "une victoire au Hamas"
france24fr.description: Annoncé dimanche soir, le rejet par Israël du plan de paix américain pour Gaza traduit les dissensions au sein de la coalition gouvernementale de Benjamin Netanyahu alors que se profilent des élections législatives décisives en octobre. Selon plusieurs analystes, le Premier ministre israélien offre par ce refus une victoire diplomatique au Hamas.

france24fr.title: Syrie : Bachar al-Assad condamné à mort par contumace
france24fr.description: Un tribunal syrien a condamné mardi en son absence le président déchu Bachar al-Assad, son frère Maher et plusieurs autres ex-responsables à la peine de mort pour les crimes commis durant la guerre civile, les premières condamnations de membres de l'ancien pouvoir.

france24fr.title: Profession DJ au Pakistan : les femmes se mettent aux platines
france24fr.description: Le Pakistan, pays réputé pour ses valeurs conservatrices, fait rarement parler de lui pour sa scène musicale et de divertissement. Pourtant, dans les grandes villes comme Karachi et Lahore, une scène DJ discrète mais en plein essor commence à se faire entendre, avec des talents émergents et des artistes qui transforment l’industrie musicale. Au cœur de cette évolution, de plus en plus de femmes s’affirment dans un milieu largement dominé par les hommes.

france24fr.title: Sécheresse et canicules : l’Europe connaît sa période juin-juillet la plus chaude jamais enregistrée
france24fr.description: L’Europe occidentale vient de connaître sa période juin-juillet la plus chaude jamais mesurée, selon le service européen Copernicus. La température moyenne sur ces deux mois a atteint 21,62 °C, dépassant le précédent record établi en 2022. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Séisme en Colombie : "Nous sommes à la rue, nous n’avons nulle part où aller"
france24fr.description: Un séisme de magnitude 7,4 a frappé lundi la Colombie, dans le département pauvre du Choco, dans l’ouest du pays. Le bilan fait état mardi d'au moins 224 morts, de centaines de blessés, ainsi que de nombreux dégâts matériels. France 24 a recueilli les témoignages de plusieurs habitants de la ville de Quibdo.

france24fr.title: Colombie : les opérations de sauvetage se poursuivent après le séisme
france24fr.description: En Colombie, les opérations de sauvetage se poursuivent dans l'ouest du pays, frappé lundi par un séisme de magnitude 7,4 - le plus puissant que le pays ait subi depuis ​des décennies. Récit de Noémie Roche.

france24fr.title: France : l'éclipse solaire dope le tourisme, Biarritz se prépare à un spectacle presque total
france24fr.description: À la veille de l’éclipse solaire du 12 août, Biarritz se prépare à accueillir de nombreux curieux. Dans cette ville du sud de la France, la Lune masquera jusqu’à 99,5% du Soleil, soit le taux d’occultation le plus élevé observé depuis la France métropolitaine. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Face aux "Aperçus IA" de Google, les quotidiens français saisissent l'Autorité de la concurrence
france24fr.description: L'Alliance ​de ‌la presse d'information générale, organisme collectif regroupant près de 300 quotidiens français, a annoncé mardi être passée à l'offensive devant l'Autorité de la concurrence après le déploiement fin juillet par Google de résumés réalisés par IA, dont les médias redoutent qu'ils ne les privent de trafic.

france24fr.title: En Côte d’Ivoire, Laurent Gbagbo délègue une partie de ses pouvoirs à cinq cadres du PPA-CI
france24fr.description: En Côte d’Ivoire, Laurent Gbagbo délègue une partie de ses prérogatives à cinq cadres du PPA-CI, tout en conservant la présidence du parti. Une réorganisation qui relance une question : lequel de ces cinq responsables pourrait incarner l’après-Gbagbo ?

france24fr.title: Canada : état d'urgence et évacuations par milliers, au moins 612 feux actifs recensés
france24fr.description: Le Canada fait face à une saison des incendies particulièrement intense. 612 feux de forêt sont actuellement actifs à travers le pays, dont une centaine en Colombie-Britannique, où plusieurs incendies restent hors de contrôle. Pour en parler, France 24 reçoit le commandant Sebti Khadimallah, porte-parole de la Sécurité civile et de la gestion des crises.

france24fr.title: Une attaque des Houthis sur un navire en mer Rouge fait plusieurs morts
france24fr.description: ⁠Un cargo a ⁠été attaqué ​mardi par les Houthis dans le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, causant ​la mort dequatre membres d'équipage, ont déclaré mardi les autorités yéménites.

france24fr.title: Trump aurait changé d’avion après le sommet de l’Otan à Ankara
france24fr.description: Le Washington Post rapporte que le président américain Donald Trump a quitté Ankara à bord d'un avion militaire spécial après le sommet de l'OTAN le mois dernier, alors même que la Maison Blanche laissait croire qu'il avait embarqué à bord d'Air Force One. En cause : des menaces iraniennes jugées crédibles. Explications avec Noémie Roche et Delano D'Souza.

france24fr.title: Guinée : un "visa médical" numérique centralise les données de santé
france24fr.description: En Guinée, pour améliorer le suivi des patients, une start-up a développé une carte numérique. Baptisée "Visa médical", elle centralise l’ensemble des données de santé du patient et les partage avec les soignants. Une innovation qui entend faciliter le suivi médical et renforcer l’efficacité des soins. Reportage de Malick Diakité, Aminatou Diallo et Sarah Sakho.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : Gbagbo délègue ses pouvoirs pour "poursuivre le combat politique"
france24fr.description: Pour renforcer le fonctionnement du Parti des peuples africains-Côte d’Ivoire, Laurent Gbagbo entend partager certaines responsabilités au sein de la direction. L’ancien chef de l’État déléguera une partie de ses prérogatives à cinq cadres du PPA-CI, tout en restant président du parti. Correspondance de M’ma Camara, à Abidjan.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Le Liban vote l'abolition de la peine de mort, une première au Moyen-Orient
Le Liban vote l'abolition de la peine de mort, une première au Moyen-Orient
france24fr.description: Le parlement libanais a voté mardi l'abolition de la peine de mort, une première au Moyen-Orient, dans une décision qualifiée d'"historique" par le ministre de la Justice Adel Nassar.

france24fr.title: L'épidémie d'Ebola a fait plus de 2 000 morts en RD Congo depuis mai
france24fr.description: L’épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola, qui continue de progresser en RD Congo, a fait depuis le mois de mai 2 011 morts, pour 4 381 cas confirmés, selon un dernier bilan publié par les autorités congolaises mardi 11 août.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : l’OMS appelle à un essai clinique du vaccin Ervebo
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, l’épidémie d’Ebola progresse à une vitesse inédite et dépasse désormais les 4 000 cas déclarés. Face au variant Bundibugyo, l’OMS appelle à un essai clinique du vaccin Ervebo, seul vaccin disponible contre Ebola.

nzz.title: David gegen Goliath im Swissness-Streit: Kybun-Joya verlagert Produktion nach Italien, On freut sich auf das Schweizerkreuz
nzz.description: Der Streit um das Schweizerkreuz entwickelt sich zu einem Kampf zwischen KMU und Grosskonzernen. Der Gewerbeverband warnt vor einer Verlagerung von Arbeitsplätzen ins Ausland.

nzz.title: Der Kanton will den Hochwasserschutz an der Sihl vorantreiben. Doch wegen der Trockenheit gerät das Projekt ins Stocken
nzz.description: Mit dem Entlastungsstollen will sich der Kanton gegen Überschwemmungen schützen. In diesen Tagen steht er jedoch vor einem Dilemma.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Selbstherrliche Polizeikader, fehlende Führung, amateurhafte Kommunikation: Die Finanzaffäre in Uster zeigt ein Versagen auf der ganzen Linie
nzz.description: Die Stadtregierung müsste reinen Tisch machen. Stattdessen begeht sie einen Fehler nach dem anderen. Jetzt braucht es eine parlamentarische Untersuchung.

nzz.title: Cassis verteidigt die flexible Neutralität: Nur so könne die Schweiz «angemessen auf neue Herausforderungen reagieren»
nzz.description: Ende September stimmt die Bevölkerung über die Neutralitätsinitiative ab. Am Dienstag erklärte der Aussenminister, weshalb der Bundesrat die Vorlage ablehnt.

nzz.title: Harry-Potter-Fans bewirken die Verlegung eines millionenteuren Unterseestromkabels
nzz.description: An einem Strand in Wales sollte die Leitung eines riesigen Stromprojekts mitten durch das «Grab» der Filmfigur Dobby verlaufen. Doch Hunderte Fans intervenierten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Westen darf Myanmar nicht so einfach abschreiben
nzz.description: Myanmar steckt seit fünf Jahren im Bürgerkrieg. Weder die Junta noch die Rebellenarmeen erringen den eindeutigen Sieg. Der Westen sollte die Hoffnung auf ein geeintes, demokratisches Myanmar aber beibehalten – aus Eigeninteresse.

nzz.title: Ein Orban-Kritiker wird neuer Staatspräsident in Ungarn
nzz.description: Das Parlament hat den international angesehenen Juristen Andras Baka zum Staatsoberhaupt gewählt. Der Regierungschef Magyar hofft, damit den Wirbel um das Präsidentenamt beenden zu können.

nzz.title: Boxpromoter und mutmasslicher Chef eines Drogenimperiums: Wer ist Daniel Kinahan, Irlands wohl gefährlichster Gangsterboss?
nzz.description: Kinahan soll mit seiner Organisation jahrelang den Drogen- und Waffenschmuggel in Irland und darüber hinaus kontrolliert haben. Nun haben ihn die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate nach Irland ausgeliefert. Dort droht ihm lebenslange Haft.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Kolumbiens Präsident ruft nach Erdbeben der Stärke 7,4 den Notstand aus: Zahl der Toten steigt auf mehr als 220
nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat am Montag Kolumbien erschüttert. Zahlreiche Gebäude stürzten ein und die Zahl der Verletzten könnte sich auf mehrere Hunderte belaufen. Die wichtigsten Antworten.

nzz.title: Libanons Parlament schafft die Todesstrafe ab
nzz.description: Mit der Abschaffung ist der Libanon das erste arabische Land, das die Todesstrafe formell aus seinem Strafrecht streicht. Der Hizbullah stimmte dagegen.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Nach Jahren mit roten Zahlen schreibt das Unispital wieder Gewinne
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Wie Russlands Militär ein Bein in Syrien behält und warum Damaskus nicht ganz mit Moskau bricht
nzz.description: Russland war jahrelang der wichtigste Verbündete des gestürzten Diktators Bashar al-Asad. Trotzdem hat Syriens neue Regierung jetzt ein militärisches Kooperationsabkommen mit Moskau geschlossen. Sie hat dafür gute Gründe.

nzz.title: Nur wenige Tage im Amt – und schon muss der Präsident Kolumbiens eine Katastrophe bewältigen
nzz.description: Das schwere Erdbeben in Kolumbien fordert mindestens 224 Tote und ist eine erste Prüfung für die neue Rechtsregierung. Diese kann indes auf ihre Verbündeten in der Region und in Washington zählen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Pegelstände des Rheins fallen weiter – Rekordtief in Köln +++ Deutsche müssen nach Waldbrand aufs Duschen verzichten
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: Ätna hochaktiv – Tausende Touristen gestrandet
nzz.description: Mitten in der Hauptreisezeit sorgt Europas grösster Vulkan mit seinen Ausbrüchen für grosse Probleme. In Catania kann am Dienstagmorgen nur eine einzige Maschine starten. Touristen sind verzweifelt.

observador.title: Polícias reforçam segurança na Baixa após turista baleada
observador.description: O MAI anunciou mais policiamento na baixa e zonas turísticas de Lisboa. Uma mulher de 40 anos foi baleada na segunda-feira alegadamente por dois suspeitos ligados ao tráfico de droga.

observador.title: As relações amorosas têm "atualizações" durante as férias?
observador.description: Sai da rotina, muda o cenário, sobra mais tempo a dois. Será que as férias funcionam como um "teste" às relações amorosas, revelando coisas que o dia-a-dia disfarça?

observador.title: Parque Logístico de Grândola avança em 2027
observador.description: Responsáveis visam iniciar "imediatamente" obras de infraestruturas. Novas captações de água são obstáculo, mas previstas na conceção do projeto. 40 milhões de euros em investimento direto.

observador.title: Enfermeiros exigem unidade de oncologia no Santo António
observador.description: Falta de vagas em hematologia obriga internamentos dispersos. Sindicato dos Enfermeiros quer ainda corrigir avaliações em atraso desde 2023 e aplicação de benesses de penosidade.

observador.title: Seguro quer nova forma de olhar para territórios e empresas
observador.description: O Presidente da República defendeu, na Covilhã, que Portugal precisa de descentralizar decisões e de crescer o tecido empresarial para reter jovens qualificados.

observador.title: Exames. Ministro acusado de fugir a responsabilidades
observador.description: O Movimento Escola Pública considerou o inquérito "uma falta de respeito para com os professores". Já o cossecretário-geral da Fenprof acusou Fernando Alexandre de querer ter "bodes expiatórios".

observador.title: Eclipse pode mudar o tempo: mais frio e vento e menos nuvens
observador.description: A costa entre Coimbra e o Minho, o Grande Porto e a Grande Lisboa são de risco para ver o eclipse: terão nuvens baixas. O interior e todo o sul estão limpos, mas com aviso amarelo para calor de 40ºC.

observador.title: Aldeia envelhecida com resort de 3 milhões de investimento
observador.description: Com investimento de 3 milhões a 28 de agosto vai abrir um resort em Virela, "uma aldeia envelhecida na freguesia de Arcozelo das Maias", no concelho de Oliveira de Frades.

observador.title: Sérvulo. "Ainda sou um verdadeiro social-democrata”.
observador.description: Sérvulo Correia recorda os tempos de dirigente nacional do PSD, de membro do VI Governo Provisório e das razões para romper com o PSD de Sá Carneiro. Segunda parte de uma longa conversa com Luís Rosa.

observador.description: O internacional sub-21 português saiu ao minuto 36 do Rangers-Hibernian (1-2). Após avaliação, o clube confirmou lesão grave no joelho com paragem prolongada.

observador.description: Deputados húngaros do partido do atual primeiro-ministro húngaro Péter Magyar elegeram um novo Presidente, que tinha alvo de uma "purga" por Viktor Orbán. No discurso inaugural, Baka criticou ex-PM

observador.description: Há também registo de cerca de três mil desaparecidos. Ainda, a saída de professores para reforma preocupa a FENPROF e amanhã todos os jovens têm entrada gratuita nos museus e monumentos nacionais.

observador.title: Marquês. Corrupção só prescreve em dezembro de 2028, diz MP
observador.description: Defesas de administradores de Vale do Lobo pedem ao tribunal o reconhecimento da prescrição, que pode servir também a Sócrates e Vara. Procuradores contestam e apontam prescrições para 2028 e 2033.

observador.title: Polícia angolana: Força moderada para dispersar manifestação
observador.description: A polícia angolana garante que usou meios não letais para dispersar manifestantes da UNITA que se juntaram num "local proibido por lei" e que "houve apenas ferimentos ligeiros por escoriação".

observador.title: Alforrecas quase paralisam maior central nuclear de França
observador.description: O surgimento de uma grande quantidade destes animais marinhos começou a obstruir as bombas utilizadas para arrefecimento, obrigando os responsáveis a ativar protocolos de segurança.

observador.title: Queda de cabelo na mulher: da gravidez à menopausa
observador.description: A queda capilar feminina é uma das queixas mais frequentes. Os dermatologistas Dr. António Massa e Dra. Filipa Ventura falam sobre causas e o impacto emocional de um problema mal compreendido.

observador.title: Três carteiristas detidos por furto a turistas no Porto
observador.description: A PSP deteve três alegados carteiristas pelo furto de duas malas, que continham 705 euros e uns AirPods. A polícia consegui interceptou os suspeitos após seguir a localização dos auriculares.

Le duo, 100% fribourgeois, quatrième par équipe aux Jeux olympiques de Paris, participe cette semaine à ses derniers Championnats du monde de concours complet. Le dernier chapitre d’une sacrée épopée qui a mis en lumière un sport encore méconnu et peu doté

letemps.description:
Dans les trois nouvelles du recueil, toutes situées dans un bourg imaginaire proche du Canada, l’écrivain fait souffler les braises qui sommeillent sous la paisible surface des choses

letemps.description:
Edgar Selge, né en 1948, retrace avec distance et sensibilité le difficile adieu au nazisme d’une famille allemande, la sienne. Ce premier livre d’un grand acteur est une réussite qui allie deuil et humour

Acteur célèbre en Allemagne, Edgar Selge s’est mis à l’écriture à plus de 70 ans pour reconstituer son histoire familiale, entre souvenirs et fiction, et c’est une magnifique réussite.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Token Economy Requires Collective Data Governance
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.
